kruer-kohlmeyer-price-2026.title: Unit distances in convex polygons

local.notes: Supplied local PDF copied from prove2me/submissions/negative-resolution-20260913/upstream/96-97.pdf; SHA-256 0aa734bee7dd050157f6423b5869e78ea469406c81a91f64e1f97c5b38d5c818.

claims.claim: The manuscript gives U_c(n) = Ω(n log log n) for strictly convex n-point sets.
claims.source_says: Theorem 1.1 gives min{δ₁(P), u(P)/n} ≥ 1/4 log log n − C log log log n for every sufficiently large n; Corollary 1.2 states U_c(n) = Ω(n log log n).

claims.claim: The manuscript gives arbitrarily large fixed minimum unit-distance degree at every sufficiently large cardinality.
claims.source_says: Corollary 1.2 states that for every integer k ≥ 1 and every sufficiently large n there is a strictly convex n-point set in which every point has at least k unit-distance neighbours; Proposition 4.3 supplies the construction for n ≥ M_k².

claims.claim: The manuscript supplies a Problem 97 counterexample with k = 4 and at most 3432·2^36036 vertices.
claims.source_says: Corollary 4.4 states the bound; its proof sets k = 4, d = 7, q = 8 and computes N₇,₈ = 3432·2^36036.
